title: Greedy Announcement Distribution with Cost Threshold
approach_explanation: The problem asks for the minimum cost to notify all $n$ residents. Pak Chanek can either notify a resident directly with cost $p$, or a resident can notify up to $a_i$ other residents at cost $b_i$ per share. To minimize the cost, we should always prefer using residents with the cheapest sharing cost $b_i$, provided $b_i < p$. If the cheapest available sharing cost is greater than or equal to $p$, it is always cheaper or equal to directly notify the remaining residents using $p$. Thus, we can sort the residents based on their sharing cost $b_i$ in ascending order and greedily fulfill the required notifications using the cheapest sharing options until all residents are notified or no more beneficial sharing options remain.

code_breakdown.explanation: Read the number of test cases $t$, and for each test case read $n$ and $p$, along with arrays $a$ (maximum shares per person) and $b$ (cost per share).
Create an index array and sort it based on the corresponding values in array $b$ in ascending order using a custom comparator.

Initialize the cost with $p$ (assuming at least one person must be directly notified by Pak Chanek) and count = 1. Iterate through the sorted indices and use residents with $b[idx] < p$ to cover as many remaining people as possible. If $b[idx] 
mid p$, break and pay $p$ for all remaining unnotified residents.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: Reading the input takes $O(n)$ time. Sorting the indices of size $n$ takes $O(n \log n)$ time. The greedy loop iterates at most $n$ times. Summing over all test cases, the total time complexity is bounded by $O(\sum n \log n)$, which easily fits within the 1-second time limit for $\sum n \leq 10^5$.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: Vectors $a$, $b$, and $min\_index$ each take $O(n)$ space to store the attributes for the residents.

strengths: Efficient use of sorting and greedy choice property.
Handles large constraints appropriately using `long long` for cost calculations to prevent integer overflow.
Clear modular flow per test case.
edge_cases_handled: $p$ being very small or very large compared to $b_i$ elements.
Early termination when all residents are notified.

optimization_and_alternatives.tradeoffs: Instead of sorting an index array, one can sort a vector of custom structures/pairs containing $(b_i, a_i)$, which simplifies memory layout and code readability slightly.
